deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 45-47 of cote 154): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial model for an arrangement Σ of n pseudo-lines D_i. The model consists of the following data.
- A surface X with a map φ: X → Y.
- φ is an immersion on each face of (X,K).
- K is the critical (fold) graph. Near ordinary points of K, φ is an ordinary fold; at vertices of K it is a 'double folding'.
- L = φ^{-1}(∪D_i), the pulled-back arrangement.
- K has ordinary and exceptional edges and components. Previous page: stable, instable or semi-stable exceptional edges, and the 'bord privilégié' at critical points.

This page is an outline of section headings l), m), n) plus two NBs.

(l) A 'law of symmetrization' around an exceptional edge, and the local structure of (X, K∪L) near an exceptional component of K. The large coloured figure shows a band along a horizontal axis (green/brown: an exceptional component of K). Yellow-green vertical lines are transverse pieces of K. Orange curves are the L-strands. The figure shows them mirrored across the axis, with lens-shaped bigons appearing symmetrically above and below; small crosses mark vertices.

NB on numerics: the index of an exceptional edge a with endpoints s0, s1 is n − (ν_{s0} − 1) − (ν_{s1} − 1), where ν_s is the multiplicity at the vertex (number of strands through it). An earlier inequality '≤ n − ν' is marked 'correction!'. He concludes that the index of exceptional edges is determined by the other numerical data. Combinatorially this counts the strands not passing through either endpoint, keeping the strand carrying the edge itself. That is the natural count in a pseudo-line arrangement.

(m) Indexing of the sections (local branches of L, i.e. which pseudo-lines) over each face of (X,K) by an index set Ĩ, presumably the 2n oriented lines or banks ('rives', cf. p. 45). He also wants the rule for passing from the indexation on one face to that on an adjacent face.

(n) Reconstruction of the arrangement Σ (via Ĩ) from K alone plus numerical data:
- vertex indices ν(s), with integrality and parity-type conditions (2ν(s) − (…), ν(s) ∈ ℕ);
- edge indices ν(a), distinguishing ordinary and exceptional edges.
This is a 'Σ is determined by a decorated graph' statement.

Right NB. There should also be a symmetrization law across an ordinary edge, not deduced from the configuration on the two adjacent faces but from the map (X, K∪L) and a 'tubular neighbourhood' T of K∪L. He notes it does not hold for every edge of K as naively stated. Precise version (bottom right):
- T_a := (F' ∪ F'') ∩ T, where F', F'' are the two faces incident to a.
- There is an involution σ_a of T_a with fixed-point set a, respecting the cellulation induced by (X, K∪L).
- If edges a, b meet at a vertex s, then σ_a and σ_b restricted to T_a ∩ T_b satisfy a compatibility; the reading is uncertain ('commutent' or 'conjugués les uns aux autres').

The small figure illustrates the local picture at an edge between two transverse K-lines, with a dashed vertex at one end.

The next page (dated 7.2.1984) turns this into a combinatorial structure. K is subdivided by order-2 vertices coloured red and black. Faces are 4n-gons, and edges carry signs ε_F(a) with sign rules. Each edge a has a reflection σ_a^F: Pol(F) → Pol(F') fixing the 'grande arête' and swapping red and black vertices, with σ_a^F σ_a^{F'} = id. This is a reflection-group-like, Coxeter-complex-flavoured cellular structure on the folded surface.
errors: Self-corrected on the page: the bound '≤ n−ν' for indices of exceptional edges is replaced (marked 'correction!') by the exact formula n−(ν_{s0}−1)−(ν_{s1}−1). Whether the parenthetical '≤ n−ν' remark survives for vertices is unclear.

The right NB admits the ordinary-edge symmetrization is not available for every edge a of K ('Mais pas ... de toute arête a de K, pourtant'). The general claim is therefore not established; the precise hypothesis (restriction to a tubular neighbourhood T of K∪L) is only sketched.

The vertex compatibility (commutation/conjugacy of σ_a, σ_b on T_a∩T_b) is stated without proof and the reading is uncertain; for adjacent mirrors meeting at a vertex one would rather expect a dihedral relation than plain commutation, unless the angle is right.

ideas.what: Encoding a pseudo-line arrangement by a fold map φ: X→Y whose critical graph K and pulled-back arrangement L give a cellular map (X, K∪L)
ideas.modern_name: Topological representation of arrangements / oriented matroids of rank 3 via fold maps; related to wiring diagrams and Goodman–Pollack sweeps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Folkman–Lawrence (1978) for topological representation
ideas.where_published: Pseudo-line systems possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) context; unsure

ideas.what: Local reflection involution σ_a on a tubular neighbourhood of each edge of the critical graph, preserving the induced cellulation, with compatibility at vertices
ideas.modern_name: Local reflection structure / Coxeter-type (mirror) structure on a folded surface; orbifold-like reflection charts
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart for pseudo-line arrangements known to me

ideas.what: Index of an exceptional edge equals n − (ν_{s0}−1) − (ν_{s1}−1), so it is determined by the vertex multiplicities
ideas.modern_name: Elementary incidence count in line arrangements

ideas.what: Reconstruction of the arrangement Σ from the graph K decorated by integer vertex/edge indices ν(s), ν(a) subject to integrality/parity conditions
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial encoding/realization of arrangements by decorated graphs (cf. local sequences, allowable sequences, cyclic sequences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences); Felsner et al. (combinatorial encodings)

ideas.what: Indexation of local branches of L on each face by an index set Ĩ (oriented lines/banks) with transition rules across edges
ideas.modern_name: Local systems / monodromy of labels on a cell complex; sign-vector (covector) labelling of oriented matroids

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes that the full pseudo-line arrangement can be reconstructed from the fold graph K plus integer indices on vertices and edges (with integrality conditions), and that the arrangement carries a system of local reflections σ_a along K compatible at vertices. This is a non-standard combinatorial-topological encoding of pseudo-line arrangements via fold singularities; the reconstruction theorem is only announced in outline.
missed.quote: Reconstitution de Σ (via Ĩ ...) à l'aide de K, et des conditions numériques ... ν(a) des arêtes de K (distinguer le cas des arêtes ordinaires et des arêtes exceptionnelles.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Encodings of pseudo-line arrangements (enumeration, flip graphs, realizability) are active topics. A fold-map/reflection-structure encoding is not, to my knowledge, in the literature and might yield a new bijection or a new invariant. However, it is only sketched, and the setup across the surrounding pages would need reconstructing.

missed.claim: Mirrors of a folded surface (fold edges carrying involutions, compatible at vertices) linked to arrangement combinatorics. This suggests a reflection-group/orbifold viewpoint on pseudo-line arrangements, made explicit on the next page as red/black-swapping reflections between 4n-gonal faces.
missed.quote: on a une involution σ_a de T_a, ayant a comme ensemble de pts fixes, ... respectant la structure des cellulations induites par (X, K∪L)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could relate pseudo-line arrangements to Coxeter complexes or reflection orbifolds in a way not standard in oriented matroid theory. This is speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working outline (section headings l–n) of an unpublished, idiosyncratic encoding of pseudo-line arrangements via fold maps with local reflection symmetries. It is interesting and seemingly absent from the literature, but mostly programmatic. The one concrete formula (exceptional edge index) is an elementary count, and the key claims are unproved and partly self-doubted.
transcription_corrections: Heading l): likely 'Loi de symétrisation autour d'une arête exceptionnelle (supposée ... fixe), et structure locale autour d'une composante exceptionnelle de K'.
m): probably 'Indexation des sections de L sur les faces de (X,K) par Ĩ, et passage d'une indexation à l'indexation de la face adjacente'.

NB right: 'pas en ... de la configuration induite par les nombres de 2 faces adjacentes'. The fragment 'carte (X, K∪L)' (map/carte) seems to be what is written, followed by 'le voisinage "tubulaire" ... de K∪L dans cette carte' — reading tentative.

Bottom right: 'on a une involution σ_a de T_a, ayant a comme ensemble des pts fixes, et respectant la structure des cellulations induites par (X, K∪L). De plus, si a, b sont incidentes en un même sommet s, alors σ_a|T_a∩T_b et σ_b|T_a∩T_b ...'. The last verb is uncertain ('commutent' vs a relation stated 'les uns aux autres').
The word read as 'Grassi' under item n) is doubtful; it may be 'Gaussi[ennes]' or an unrelated annotation.
Left margin under the large figure: likely 'figure correcte, ...' or 'figure inexacte' rather than 'figure cumulée'.
